Top-level package¶

Stable lattice/lattice-ladder DSP filters backed by C++.

lattice-dsp is a stability-first IIR toolkit: reflection/PARCOR parameterization, lattice-ladder realizations, adaptive recursive filtering, OpenMP batch processing, and small dependency-light examples.

It is not a production acoustic echo canceller. Echo helpers are retained as synthetic ERLE/system-identification examples, not product claims.

class lattice_dsp.HybridEchoCanceller(initial_reflection, initial_taps, *, mu_taps=0.05, mu_reflection=0.001, epsilon=1e-08, margin=0.0001, freeze_reflection=False, gradient_mode='analytic', reflection_update_period=8, scale_reflection_mu_by_period=True, residual_processor=None, sample_rate=None, safety_max_power_ratio=None, safety_max_abs=None)[source]

Bases: object

Linear adaptive lattice/IIR stage plus optional residual processor.

This helper is intentionally small. It models the common hybrid strategy:

  1. a stable adaptive lattice/IIR filter estimates the linear echo path from a reference/far-end signal to the microphone signal;

  2. the residual signal is passed to an optional dependency-free processor such as a fixed attenuator, a spectral suppressor, or any callable supplied by the user.

The residual processor is called as processor(residual, context). The context dictionary contains reference, microphone, echo_estimate, sample_rate, and linear_filter.

Return the causal matrix impulse response of the online realization.

The returned array has shape (n_samples, outputs, inputs). Entry h[t, i, j] is the output in channel i at delay t after a unit impulse in input channel j. The response is truncated to the requested length; matrix-lattice all-pass responses are generally IIR, so longer lengths expose more of the decaying tail.

class lattice_dsp.OnlineMatrixLatticeAllPass(lattice)[source]

Bases: object

Causal streaming realization of MatrixLatticeAllPass.

The existing MatrixLatticeAllPass object defines the transfer function. This runtime wrapper realizes the same Schur/lattice cascade in time, with one vector delay per section. For an input vector u[n] the output at time n depends only on u[n] and previous internal states; future samples are never inspected.

The finite prefix energy of a processed block can differ from the input energy because some energy remains in the delay states. Over a long stream, or after appending enough zero samples to let the tail decay, the input-output energy agrees up to numerical precision for a lossless/all-pass lattice.

Parameters:

lattice (MatrixLatticeAllPass)

Reset all section delay states to zero.

Return type:

class lattice_dsp.MIMOLatticePredictor(forward_reflection, backward_reflection)[source]

Bases: object

Causal online multichannel lattice predictor.

The predictor implements the vector lattice recursion

f_0[n] = b_0[n] = y[n]

f_m[n] = f_{m-1}[n] + K_m b_{m-1}[n-1]

b_m[n] = b_{m-1}[n-1] + L_m f_{m-1}[n]

where K_m and L_m are forward and backward matrix reflection coefficients. Calling predict() uses only the stored backward-error state from previous samples and therefore gives y_hat[n] before y[n] is observed. Calling update() then consumes the observed vector and returns the forward prediction error.

The class is a runtime filter/predictor. Estimating the reflection matrices with block_levinson_durbin() is a separate batch operation.

Parameters:

  • forward_reflection (ArrayLike)

  • backward_reflection (ArrayLike)

class lattice_dsp.MultichannelARResult(coefficients, prediction_error, reflection, backward_coefficients, backward_error, method, backward_reflection=None)[source]

Bases: object

Result returned by multichannel AR solvers.

Parameters:

  • coefficients (numpy.ndarray) – AR coefficient matrices with shape (order, channels, channels). The model convention is x[n] + sum_j A[j] @ x[n-j-1] = e[n].

  • prediction_error (numpy.ndarray) – Forward prediction-error covariance matrix.

  • reflection (numpy.ndarray) – Forward matrix reflection / partial-correlation coefficients. For the direct dense solver this is empty because reflection coefficients are an order-recursive quantity.

  • backward_coefficients (numpy.ndarray) – Backward AR coefficient matrices from the block Levinson recursion.

  • backward_error (numpy.ndarray) – Backward prediction-error covariance matrix.

  • method (str) – Human-readable solver label.

  • backward_reflection (numpy.ndarray | None) – Backward matrix reflection coefficients used by causal multichannel lattice prediction. Direct dense solvers leave this empty.

lattice_dsp.block_levinson_durbin(r, order=None, *, regularization=0.0)[source]

Estimate a vector AR model with the block Levinson-Durbin recursion.

This implements the forward/backward block recursion often associated with multichannel Levinson, Whittle, and Wiggins-Robinson/LWR algorithms. It returns the same forward AR coefficients as the dense block Yule-Walker solve for well-conditioned covariance sequences, while also exposing the order-recursive matrix reflection coefficients.

Parameters:

  • r (ndarray | Iterable[float] | Iterable[complex])

  • order (int | None)

  • regularization (float)

Return type:

MultichannelARResult

Right tangential Schur interpolation data.

The data describe matrix-valued Schur functions

S : D -> C^{output_dim x input_dim}

satisfying

S(z_i) U_i = V_i.

U_i is an input_dim x r_i direction matrix and V_i is an output_dim x r_i target matrix. A common rank-one input accepts arrays with shape (points, input_dim) and (points, output_dim).

Parameters:

  • points (ndarray)

  • directions (tuple[ndarray, ...])

  • values (tuple[ndarray, ...])

output_dim: int

Number of interpolation nodes.

Tangential multiplicity at each node.

Total number of tangential columns across all nodes.

class lattice_dsp.TangentialPotapovFactor(point, input_direction, output_value, *, strict_tol=1e-12)[source]

Bases: object

Elementary J-inner factor associated with one strict tangential vector.

For xi = [v; u] and J = diag(I_output, -I_input), strict Schur data satisfy xi^* J xi < 0. The factor

Theta(z) = I + (b_alpha(z) - 1) P

uses the J-orthogonal projection P onto span(xi) and is J-inner on the unit circle. At z = alpha it annihilates the data vector xi.

  • input_direction (ndarray)

  • output_value (ndarray)

  • strict_tol (float)

lattice_dsp.experimental_mimo_state_space_to_matrix_lattice(A, B, C, D, *, order, n_markov=256, n_freq=256, candidate_gains=None, fit_static_gains=False, static_gain_mode='both', static_gain_iterations=20, margin=1e-06, n_threads=0)[source]

Experimental square MIMO state-space to matrix-lattice all-pass fit.

The fitted object is a MatrixLatticeAllPass, so the target is the unitary/polar part of the state-space response, not the full nonunitary gain response. The routine builds Markov-initialized lattice scaffolds for a grid of reflection gains and returns the candidate with the smallest relative Frobenius error against the target polar factor. When fit_static_gains is true, the routine also fits static left/right gain matrices around the selected lattice response, H(w) ~= L @ G_lattice(w) @ R. This separates all-pass scaffold quality from nonunitary static gain mismatch.

This is a practical diagnostic/initializer for matrix-lattice realization experiments. It is not a full matrix AAK/Nehari solver and it is not a proof that an arbitrary stable MIMO state-space model has been exactly realized in matrix-lattice coordinates.

Parameters:

  • A (ndarray | Sequence[Sequence[float]])

  • B (ndarray | Sequence[Sequence[float]])

  • fit_static_gains (bool)

lattice_dsp.fit_static_matrix_gains(target_response, lattice_response, *, mode='both', n_iter=20, regularization=1e-12)[source]

Fit static matrix gains around a matrix-lattice response.

The model is

target_response[w] ~= left_gain @ lattice_response[w] @ right_gain.

mode='left' fixes right_gain = I; mode='right' fixes left_gain = I; mode='both' alternates least-squares updates for both factors. This is a diagnostic used to separate all-pass/lattice mismatch from static nonunitary gain mismatch. It is not a dynamic realization solver.

Parameters:

lattice_dsp.matrix_lattice_finite_adjoint(y, impulse_response, *, output_length=None)[source]

Apply the finite-block adjoint of a truncated causal MIMO response.

If h[k] denotes a causal matrix impulse response, forward convolution is

y[n] = sum_k h[k] x[n-k].

This helper applies the corresponding finite-block adjoint

x_adj[n] = sum_k h[k]^H y[n+k]

using only time-domain sums. The operation is generally noncausal as a synthesis/inverse step because it depends on future output samples. It is intended for finite-record diagnostics such as paraunitary reconstruction tests, where the whole transformed record is available.

Parameters:

  • y (ndarray | Sequence[Sequence[complex]])

  • impulse_response (ndarray | Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[complex]]])

  • output_length (int | None)

Return type:

ndarray

Bases: object

Parameters:

gain (float)

class lattice_dsp.SpectralResidualSuppressor(*, frame_size=512, hop_size=None, mode='echo_aware', floor=0.08, over_subtract=1.25, noise_percentile=20.0, smoothing=0.65, exponent=1.0, echo_aware_strength=0.7, reference_key='echo_estimate', echo_gate=False, echo_gate_threshold=0.05, echo_gate_transition=0.2, echo_gate_floor=0.0, epsilon=1e-10)[source]

Bases: object

Small deterministic STFT-domain residual echo suppressor.

This class is intentionally not a production denoiser. It provides a reproducible, dependency-free residual-model baseline beyond the toy gain attenuator.

By default the suppressor is echo-aware when a context dictionary with reference or echo_estimate is supplied. It estimates time-frequency coherence between the residual and the echo/reference signal, then attenuates components that remain correlated with the far-end path. This is safer for echo-cancellation benchmarks than blind spectral gating, because near-end speech/noise should be preserved when it is not coherent with the far-end.

If no useful context is supplied, the class falls back to a blind STFT soft gate. The blind mode is useful as a denoising sanity check but can damage the desired near-end target and should not be interpreted as residual echo suppression.

Parameters:

  • frame_size (int) – STFT frame length. If the signal is shorter, it is padded internally.

  • hop_size (int | None) – Frame hop. Defaults to one quarter of frame_size.

  • mode (str) – "echo_aware" uses far-end/echo coherence when context is available; "blind" always uses the old percentile-floor soft gate.

  • floor (float) – Minimum gain. A value of 0 can create artifacts; 0.05 to 0.2 is usually safer for examples.

  • over_subtract (float) – Blind-mode multiplier applied to the estimated residual floor.

  • noise_percentile (float) – Blind-mode percentile across time used as the residual floor estimate.

  • smoothing (float) – Temporal gain smoothing in [0, 1). Larger values vary more slowly.

  • exponent (float) – Optional gain curve exponent. In echo-aware mode this is applied to the coherence before suppression; in blind mode it shapes the soft gate.

  • echo_aware_strength (float) – Suppression strength for coherence-based echo-aware mode.

  • reference_key (str) – Preferred context key for the far-end/echo-correlated signal. If this key is absent, echo_estimate and then reference are tried.

  • echo_gate (bool) – If true, scale echo-aware suppression by a block-level echo-confidence estimate. This helps real-audio/double-talk cases where the residual is dominated by near-end content and a fixed global suppression strength can over-suppress the target.

  • echo_gate_threshold (float) – Echo-confidence threshold below which suppression is reduced toward echo_gate_floor.

  • echo_gate_transition (float) – Width of the soft transition from reduced to full suppression.

  • echo_gate_floor (float) – Minimum fraction of echo_aware_strength kept when the gate is closed.

  • epsilon (float)

process(signal)[source]

lattice_dsp.finite_aak_siso_certificate(tail, *, rank, rows, cols, criteria=None)[source]

Build a finite-section SISO AAK/Nehari diagnostic certificate.

This routine is the first “true AAK/Nehari” bridge in the package: it uses the Schmidt-pair equations for the finite Hankel matrix directly. For a chosen target rank r, it reports the first neglected singular value sigma_next, verifies the finite Schmidt-pair identities

H v = sigma_next u and H.T u = sigma_next v,

and attaches the existing finite Nehari/rational candidate for the same rank. It is still a finite-section diagnostic, not a full infinite Hardy-space AAK/Nehari solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • rank (int)

  • rows (int)

  • cols (int)

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None)

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

lattice_dsp.finite_aak_reduce_iir(reflection, numerator, *, ranks, n_impulse, rows, cols, criteria=None, attach_certificate=True)[source]

Reduce a stable SISO lattice/IIR model with the finite AAK workflow.

This helper applies finite_aak_reduce_tail() to the causal impulse response of a stable SISO lattice/IIR model. The selected rational tail model is returned as numerator/denominator coefficients and, when stable in scalar lattice coordinates, as reflection coefficients.

Parameters:

  • reflection (Any) – Reflection/PARCOR coefficients of the full stable SISO denominator.

  • numerator (Any) – Numerator coefficients of the full SISO IIR model.

  • ranks (Iterable[int]) – Candidate rational orders to evaluate.

  • n_impulse (int) – Number of impulse-response samples used for the finite-section problem.

  • rows (int) – Finite Hankel dimensions. The impulse response must contain at least rows + cols - 1 samples.

  • cols (int) – Finite Hankel dimensions. The impulse response must contain at least rows + cols - 1 samples.

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None) – Candidate acceptance thresholds. If omitted, conservative defaults are used.

  • attach_certificate (bool) – Whether to attach a finite Schmidt-pair certificate for the selected rank.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Notes

This routine is still finite-section and diagnostic. It is useful for stable SISO IIR experiments, but it is not a full infinite-dimensional AAK/Nehari solver.

lattice_dsp.finite_aak_reduce_tail(tail, *, ranks, rows, cols, criteria=None, attach_certificate=True)[source]

Select a finite-section SISO AAK/Nehari rational reduction candidate.

This is the highest-level finite-section helper in the current package. It evaluates several finite Nehari/rational candidates, selects the first one that satisfies the supplied accuracy and pole-radius criteria, and optionally attaches a finite Schmidt-pair certificate for the selected rank.

The routine is intentionally named finite_aak_* rather than aak_reduce_iir. It is a finite-section SISO diagnostic/reduction workflow built from Hankel matrices, Schmidt-pair checks, and rational recurrence fitting. It is not a full infinite-dimensional Hardy-space AAK/Nehari solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • ranks (Iterable[int])

  • rows (int)

  • cols (int)

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None)

  • attach_certificate (bool)

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

lattice_dsp.fit_rational_tail(tail, order)[source]

Fit a scalar recurrence/IIR model to a tail sequence.

For a sequence g[n] generated by a stable rational model, there are coefficients a_1, ..., a_p such that

g[n] + a_1 g[n-1] + ... + a_p g[n-p] ≈ 0.

This routine estimates the recurrence by least squares and returns a scalar IIR denominator, numerator, and poles. It is a practical finite-data rational bridge, not a standalone AAK solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • order (int)

Return type:

dict[str, ndarray]

lattice_dsp.generate_echo_problem(*, samples=64000, sample_rate=16000, seed=1234, reflection=(0.35, -0.25, 0.15, -0.08), taps=(0.2, -0.1, 0.05, 0.0, 0.75), nonlinear_strength=0.08, nonlinearity='tanh', near_end_power_ratio=0.02, noise_snr_db=30.0, double_talk=True)[source]

Generate a reproducible synthetic nonlinear echo problem.

The linear path is stable because it is parameterized by reflection coefficients. The nonlinear component is intentionally small; the goal is to make the linear lattice/IIR stage useful while leaving a residual that a spectral or downstream residual processor could handle later.

lattice_dsp.tune_reflection_update_period(x, desired, *, periods=(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), initial_reflection=None, initial_taps=None, order=None, mu_taps=0.05, mu_reflection=0.001, epsilon=1e-08, margin=0.0001, tail=None, repeats=1, max_tail_mse_ratio=1.5, max_worst_tail_mse_ratio=None, min_stability_margin=0.05, prefer='fastest', gradient_mode='analytic', scale_reflection_mu_by_period=True, min_trials_for_robust=2)[source]

Tune reflection_update_period for adaptive lattice-ladder NLMS.

Parameters:

  • x (Any) – Either 1-D arrays with shape (samples,) or 2-D arrays with shape (trials, samples). With 2-D data, each row is treated as an independent validation trial, and max_worst_tail_mse_ratio is evaluated across rows.

  • desired (Any) – Either 1-D arrays with shape (samples,) or 2-D arrays with shape (trials, samples). With 2-D data, each row is treated as an independent validation trial, and max_worst_tail_mse_ratio is evaluated across rows.

  • periods (Iterable[int]) – Candidate denominator/reflection update periods.

  • initial_reflection (Sequence[float] | None) – Initial model parameters. If no reflection/taps are provided, a zero-initialized order-4 model is used so the convenience API works out of the box. For real experiments, pass order or explicit initial coefficients.

  • initial_taps (Sequence[float] | None) – Initial model parameters. If no reflection/taps are provided, a zero-initialized order-4 model is used so the convenience API works out of the box. For real experiments, pass order or explicit initial coefficients.

  • order (int | None) – Initial model parameters. If no reflection/taps are provided, a zero-initialized order-4 model is used so the convenience API works out of the box. For real experiments, pass order or explicit initial coefficients.

  • max_tail_mse_ratio (float) – Constraint on the median tail-MSE ratio versus the first candidate period, typically period 1.

  • max_worst_tail_mse_ratio (float | None) – Constraint on the worst tail-MSE ratio across trials. Defaults to the same value as max_tail_mse_ratio.

  • min_trials_for_robust (int) – Minimum number of independent validation rows required before the recommendation is labelled robust. With fewer trials, the function still returns a period, but the report includes a warning that the recommendation is signal-specific.

  • prefer (str) – "fastest" chooses the fastest eligible period. "quality" / "accurate" chooses the lowest median tail MSE. "balanced" uses a simple speedup / worst-tail-ratio score.

  • mu_taps (float)

  • mu_reflection (float)

  • epsilon (float)

  • margin (float)

  • tail (int | None)

  • repeats (int)

  • min_stability_margin (float)

  • gradient_mode (str)

  • scale_reflection_mu_by_period (bool)

Returns:

A report dictionary with recommended_period, recommended, results, warnings, and metadata keys.

Return type:

dict
